questions.stem: In the following question, three statements numbered I, II and III are given. Read all the statements and determine the cause and effect relationship between them. I. In urban areas, the poor bear the brunt of environmental effects such as water or air pollution. II. The rapid urban development has outpaced the development of environmental infrastructure in many large cities. III. Just for the own sake of profit, builders in urban areas are indulge in construction work without tendering about the environment and urban poor, who mostly dies from chronical diseases.

options.a: Statement II is the cause, I and III are its effects.
options.b: Statement I is the cause, I and III are its effects.
options.c: Statement III is the cause, I and II are its effects.
options.d: Statement III is the cause and II is its effects while statement I is an effect of some independent cause.

questions.stem: Statement: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched three mega flagship schemes aimed at transforming Urban India, including the much talked about Smart Cities proposal, with a whopping Rs.4 lakh crore kitty having been lined up for the projects. Speaking at the event, Modi said, “the decision to make cities smart will be taken not by governments but by the people of the city, the local administration. options.b: Quality of life will improve in rural and urban areas.
options.c: Provision of roads and public transportation beside implementation of reforms in urban governance would be the focus under the scheme.
options.d: Millions of jobs will be created and scarcity of houses will be removed in urban and rural areas.

questions.stem: The difficulty with the proposed high-speed train line is that a used plane can be bought for one-third the price of the train line, and the plane, which is just as fast, can fly anywhere. The train would be a fixed linear system, and we live in a world that is spreading out in all directions and in which consumers choose the free-wheel systems (cars, buses, aircraft), which do not have fixed routes. Thus a sufficient market for the train will not exist. Which of the following, if true, most severely weakens the argument presented above?

options.a: Cars, buses, and planes require the efforts of drivers and pilots to guide them, whereas the train will be guided mechanically.
options.b: Cars and buses are not nearly as fast as the high-speed train will be.
options.c: Planes are not a free-wheel system because they can fly only between airports, which are less convenient for consumers than the high-speed train's stations would be.
options.d: The high-speed train line cannot use currently underutilized train stations in large cities.
options.e: For long trips, most people prefer to fly rather than to take ground-level transportation.

questions.stem: In an attempt to check its increasing pollution, Litter City has introduced a levy of Rs. 100 on every private car entering the city. Which of the following, if true, provides the best evidence that the city administration’s argument is flawed?
